page: Amazon Web Services t2.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine based on the Xen hypervisor. It runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz with 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs, configured with 1 thread per core. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory allocation, and features a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. It includes no local NVMe or SSD storage and provides no dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily in lower percentiles across compute and throughput evaluations. Single-core benchmarks such as stress-ng and Geekbench place in the bottom 10%, constrained by the processor architecture and burstable resource allocation during sustained execution. Multi-core performance metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 4707.65 and Geekbench multi-core score of 2754.0, sit in the bottom 25%. The memory architecture achieves 25.72 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 17.13 GB/sec for writes. Redis throughput measures 2.02 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 4.3 GB/sec.

Because the t2.xlarge operates on a CPU credit governance model, sustained intensive compute demands will deplete credits and throttle performance to baseline levels. This design provides cost efficiency for non-sustained workloads where processors remain largely idle between computational spikes. The instance is best suited for staging environments, development servers, code repositories, microservices, and small database applications with intermittent traffic patterns.
description: Amazon Web Services t2.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance featuring 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio, alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network capacity. The instance lacks local storage and GPU acceleration, depending on remote EBS volumes for disk operations. Benchmark results reflect entry-tier compute capabilities, with Geekbench and stress-ng scores occupying the lower quartiles due to older core architecture and burstable resource constraints. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 25.72 GB/sec, while static web throughput hits 4.3 GB/sec. The burstable credit model makes t2.xlarge cost-efficient for variable workloads with periodic spikes, though sustained intensive computation risks resource depletion. It is engineered for development servers, low-volume databases, staging environments, and intermediate batch processing tasks.
